notes: Authoritative source: official Optoma Europe ZU920T datasheet PDF (optomaeurope.com), cross-checked against optomausa.com/product/proscene-zu920t (identical connector list) and projectorcentral.com. This is a WUXGA (1920x1200) 9,800-lumen DuraCore laser installation projector - NOT a native 4K device (marketed as "4K/HDR compatible" via input signal support, i.e. accepts a 4K signal and scales it). Some secondary web snippets (e.g. from AI-search summaries) incorrectly attributed 3G-SDI and DVI-D ports to this model - the manufacturer's own spec sheet and product page confirm NO SDI and NO DVI port exists on the ZU920T; those references appear to be confusion with a different Optoma model. HDMI grade: manufacturer specifies all HDMI ports (2 in, 1 out) as "HDMI 2.0" - an earlier third-party summary claimed HDMI2 was "v1.4a" but the official Optoma datasheet lists both inputs simply as "2 x HDMI 2.0", which I've used as authoritative. The "3D sync" in/out and "12V trigger" ports are listed by the manufacturer only as connection types without specifying exact physical connector (likely mini-DIN or 3.5mm jack in practice) - mapped to the closest available connector id (dc-barrel) per instructions since no better match exists in the allowed list; treat these three ports' connector field as an approximation, not a confirmed physical connector type. AC power inlet type (IEC) was confirmed visually from the rear-panel product photo in the official datasheet (standard IEC C13/C14 inlet), since the spec sheet text only states voltage/wattage without naming the inlet type. HDBaseT input is carried over RJ45 - assigned eth-1g as a reasonable grade since HDBaseT typically operates at gigabit-class bandwidth, though this is not explicitly stated by Optoma. LAN RJ45 grade (eth-100m) is inferred as a control/network port typical of this projector class, not explicitly stated. No dedicated USB-A data/service port is listed - the single USB-A port is power-only (1.5A) for accessory power, not a host/data connection.
